title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
mutable_substrate: A complete agentic system represented as Python code: prompts, numbers and roles of foundation-model modules, control flow, loops, feedback and refinement mechanisms, memory, ensembling, tool calls, and workflows, implemented through a generated forward(taskInfo) function.
optimization_operator: A GPT-4o meta agent performs archive-conditioned program synthesis. It emits design reasoning, an agent name, and code; two self-reflection passes revise novelty and correctness, and runtime exceptions trigger up to five debugging revisions.
feedback_selection: Task accuracy, success rate, or F1 on a target-domain validation set is the fitness signal. Every refined candidate and its metric are appended to the archive; later proposals see the full archive, while top designs are selected after search for held-out testing and transfer.
archive_memory: An ever-growing archive stores baseline seeds plus every discovered agent's description, source code, and evaluation metric. It retains lower-performing stepping stones rather than only an incumbent and is inserted into the meta-agent prompt at each iteration. Empty-initialization experiments test the effect of removing human seeds.
validation_strategy: Search uses held-out validation subsets (ARC: 20; DROP/MGSM/MMLU: 128; GPQA: 32). Reported performance uses separate test sets (ARC: 60; DROP/MGSM/MMLU: 800; GPQA: 166) with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals; ARC and GPQA agents are evaluated five times, while other domains are evaluated once. The paper does not report repeated independent search runs.
adaptation_mode: Offline, domain-specific program search for 25 ARC iterations or 30 reasoning-domain iterations, followed by zero-search transfer of top architectures across datasets and foundation models. Online continual and higher-order self-improvement are proposed but not implemented.
benchmarks: ARC Public Training Set (Easy), grids no larger than 5x5, exact-match accuracy
MMLU multitask knowledge and reasoning, accuracy
Transfer to GSM8K, GSM-Hard, SVAMP, and ASDiv
ARC transfer from GPT-3.5 to Claude Haiku, GPT-4o, and Claude Sonnet
principal_results: Meta Agent Search reaches about 13.7% held-out ARC accuracy versus 8.0% for the strongest reported hand-designed baseline, with improvements emerging through archived stepping stones.
Domain-specific search reaches 79.4±0.8 F1 on DROP and 53.4±3.5% on MGSM, gains of 13.6 and 14.4 points over the strongest hand-designed medians.
It reaches 69.6±3.2% on MMLU and 34.6±3.2% on GPQA, compared with OPRO at 67.6±3.2% and 32.9±3.2%; the intervals overlap substantially.
Dynamic Role-Playing Architecture transfers from MGSM to 69.5±3.2% on GSM8K and 31.2±3.2% on GSM-Hard, beating the strongest hand-designed medians by 25.9 and 13.2 points.
Interactive Multimodal Feedback Loop transfers from MGSM to 71.9±0.8 F1 on DROP, while Structured Multimodal Feedback Loop reaches 67.0±3.2% on MMLU.
Dynamic Memory and Refinement Agent transfers from GPT-3.5 ARC search to 37.0±5.3% with GPT-4o and 48.3±5.7% with Claude Sonnet.
With an empty archive, search still beats all hand-designed medians and improves MGSM from 53.4±3.5% under seeded search to 67.5±3.3%, revealing seed-induced anchoring.
limitations: All evaluated applications are single-step question-answering tasks rather than long-horizon agents acting in interactive environments.
The demonstrated evaluator optimizes only task performance, omitting cost, latency, robustness, privacy, and safety objectives.
Turing-complete code provides theoretical expressivity but no guarantee that a finite model-guided search will cover useful regions of program space.
The paper reports bootstrap uncertainty for evaluating selected agents but not variability across independent search runs, meta-agent samples, or discovered architectures.
Validation subsets are small, especially ARC with 20 questions and GPQA with 32, creating selection-overfitting risk across 25 or 30 iterations.
Transfer superiority is best-of-search rather than uniform: individual transferred agents fall below baselines on some MMLU, GPQA, Haiku, and Sonnet comparisons.
The naive evaluator uses only terminal metrics and discards information in successful and failed execution traces.
Baseline seeds usually help but can anchor search; on MGSM, empty initialization is 14.1 points better.
Agents vary substantially in number of model calls, yet accuracy comparisons are not normalized for cost or latency.
Search costs approximately $500 for ARC and $300 per reasoning-domain run under the reported API configuration.
safety_controls: Execute all generated code inside secure, isolated containers.
Manually inspect generated programs for harmful behavior.
Publish clear warnings about risks from model-generated code.
Use a constrained framework interface and structured JSON outputs to reduce accidental malformed behavior.
No automated permission model, behavioral safety objective, adversarial test suite, or scalable replacement for manual inspection is evaluated.

explicit_predecessors.name: AI-Generating Algorithms and AutoML
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Sections 1 and 5 frame ADAS as extending learned architectures and learning algorithms from AI-GAs, AutoML, and neural architecture search to complete foundation-model agent systems.

explicit_predecessors.name: FunSearch
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Section 3 explicitly likens the constrained task of generating an agent forward function to FunSearch's use of foundation models to program candidate solutions.

explicit_predecessors.name: Open-endedness and quality-diversity algorithms
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Sections 1, 3, and 4 describe the growing archive, interestingness prompt, and recombination of low-immediate-fitness stepping stones as mechanisms related to open-ended and AI-generating algorithms.

explicit_predecessors.name: OPRO and PromptBreeder
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Sections 1 and 5 contrast their prompt-limited search spaces with whole-program design, and Section 4 compares Meta Agent Search against OPRO across four domains.

explicit_predecessors.name: DyLAN, DSPy, Trace, and GPTSwarm
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Section 5 identifies these methods as optimizing networks, combinations of predefined nodes, or graph connections while retaining more representational restrictions than general code.

explicit_predecessors.name: AgentOptimizer, AutoFlow, and Agent Symbolic Learning
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Section 5 credits these systems with learning tools, workflow languages, or prompts/tools/workflows jointly, then distinguishes Meta Agent Search through a general-purpose code substrate and foundation-model coding priors.

explicit_predecessors.name: Chain-of-Thought, Self-Refine, LLM Debate, and Quality-Diversity agents
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Sections 3 and 4 initialize the archive with these designs, evaluate them in a shared framework, and show later candidates recombining their reasoning, reflection, debate, and diversity motifs.

open_questions: How can independent search runs be compared statistically, and how stable are the discovered architectures under different meta-agent samples and models?
Can trace-aware evaluators improve credit assignment and reduce the dominant cost of repeatedly running every candidate?
How should ADAS optimize Pareto tradeoffs among accuracy, cost, latency, robustness, privacy, and safety?
Which novelty or quality-diversity mechanisms best preserve stepping stones without exhausting evaluation budgets?
How can generated tools and code be permissioned, sandboxed, audited, and released without relying on manual inspection at scale?
Do code-discovered scaffolds improve long-horizon, interactive agents under distribution shift and irreversible actions?
When do human-designed seeds accelerate search, and when do they anchor it away from better solutions?
Can one search directly for generalist architectures across multiple domains and foundation models instead of selecting domain-specific winners?
Can higher-order ADAS safely redesign its own meta agent without unstable recursive capability escalation?
How should online continual ADAS resist malicious feedback, catastrophic regressions, and self-modification of safety controls?
